div.div: مَسَوطٌ Mixed. (TA.) So in a trad. of 'Alee with Fátimeh, [in which the former expresses the intimacy of her union with him, as though they two were one person,] مَسُوطٌ لَحْمُهَا بِدَمِى وَلَحْمِى (assumed tropical:) Her flesh is blended and mixed with my blood and my flesh. (TA.) You say also, أَمْوَالُهُمْ بَيْنَهُمْ ↓ سَوِيطَةٌ Their possessions are mixed among them; (AZ, S, K;) i. q. ↓ مُسْتَوطَةٌ . (M.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
